To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the risk of adverse outcomes in patients with suspected PE is increased in the presence of low sFlt‐1 and/or high PIGF levels and that this risk is even further increased in patients with low sFlt−1/PIGF ratios.

(1) the risk of adverse outcomes was significantly higher for women who had angiogenic factor levels in the highest versus the lowest quartile, (2) the risk for adverse outcomes was significantly lower for women who had levels in the highest quartile versus women who had levels between the highest and the lowest quartiles, and (3) the risk for women who had the lowest angiogenic factor levels was significantly higher than for women who had intermediate angiogenic factor levels.
